title: Referral of Unresolved Property Charge Advance Repayment Records to a Property Charge Default Maturity Case
content:
A Property Charge Advance Repayment record in its notice period is referred only when more than the notice period, 30 calendar days, has passed since it opened with the arrearage unpaid and no arrangement chosen. Those days are counted as calendar days starting the day after the opened date, and the record is not referred on the last counted day itself. A record is also referred when its agreement was not signed in time, or when its default was not cured in time; an active At-Risk Extension holds off referral, as the product's referral-suspension term provides. Referral opens a Property Charge Default maturity case on the loan. On a HECM loan every arrangement, default and referral is reported to HUD as a property charge loss mitigation step.

## Grounds of referral

| Record's situation | Ground for referral |
|---|---|
| Notice period, more than 30 calendar days since opening, arrearage unpaid, no arrangement chosen | Yes |
| Notice period, on or before the 30th counted day | No; the record is not referred on the last counted day itself |
| Agreement not signed in time | Yes |
| Default not cured in time | Yes |

An active At-Risk Extension holds off referral.

## Notice-period boundary (hypothetical dates)

| Record opened | Last counted day (day 30) | Day under consideration | More than 30 days passed |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 June | 1 July | 1 July | No |
| 1 June | 1 July | 2 July | Yes |

The opened date that starts the count is read from the arrangement record. All three parts of the notice-period ground must hold together: the time has passed, the arrearage is unpaid, and no arrangement has been chosen.

## Effect of referral

- The record's status becomes referred, dated the referral date.
- A maturity case of the Property Charge Default type opens on the same loan, dated the referral date.
- On a HECM loan the referral is reported to HUD as a property charge loss mitigation step, as are the loan's arrangements and defaults.

The dates above are illustrative only.
